identity.title: Meet one life.
identity.body: Start with the living animal. Look, listen and move before the system opens around it.
identity.audioLabel: AMAZON FIELD AMBIENCE + DESIGNED PRESENCE · SOURCE-LABELLED

hotspots.label: JAGUAR
hotspots.detail: Ear.Rodriguez Jaguar presentation asset, CC BY 4.0. The current local proxy is presentation media, not a live animal or occurrence record.

hotspots.label: CANOPY
hotspots.detail: The 3D room creates depth around the animal. It is a designed scene, not a measured habitat reconstruction.

hotspots.label: WATER
hotspots.detail: Water becomes a visual route into habitat and relationships. This is context, not a local condition measurement.

dependency.title: Follow the relationship.
dependency.body: Leave the portrait. Trace one sourced relationship outward into prey, water and the wider living web.

hotspots.label: JAGUAR
hotspots.detail: The journey remains anchored to canonical Jaguar identity while the relationship layer expands.

hotspots.label: CAPYBARA
hotspots.detail: A sourced Jaguar–capybara relationship. Open HOW DO WE KNOW? for the exact evidence and geographic boundary.

hotspots.label: WATER
hotspots.detail: Water is shown as spatial context. Co-location alone is not presented as causation.

items.label: Relationship
items.note: Canonical relation + source boundary

items.label: Spatial context
items.note: Context only; not inferred causation

items.label: Next
items.note: Pull back from animal to ecosystem

habitat.title: The animal is not the whole story.
habitat.body: Pull back. Rivers, floodplain forest, canopy and movement corridors turn one species encounter into a living-system view.
habitat.audioLabel: WIDE CANOPY + RIVER + DISTANT FIELD AMBIENCE

hotspots.label: RIVER SYSTEM
hotspots.detail: The river is a spatial organising feature in this scene. No water-quality condition is inferred from the image.

hotspots.label: FLOODPLAIN FOREST
hotspots.detail: A habitat concept layer used to help the user see the wider system around the animal.

hotspots.label: UPPER CANOPY
hotspots.detail: The canopy is presented as part of the living place, not as a measured biodiversity inventory for this exact view.

hotspots.label: CONNECTIVITY
hotspots.detail: Connectivity is a system concept here. Any local corridor claim requires mapped evidence before publication.

items.label: Animal
items.note: One entrance into a larger system

items.label: Habitat
items.note: Place / water / connectivity context

items.label: ATLAS
items.note: Spatial inspection stays on the shared map engine

pressure.title: Now the landscape changes.
pressure.body: See fragmentation as pressure, then inspect what the evidence actually supports before moving to response.
pressure.audioLabel: REDUCED CANOPY + LOW PRESSURE BED + FIELD AMBIENCE DUCKED

hotspots.label: FRAGMENTATION
hotspots.detail: Fragmentation is used as a pressure concept. This frame is not a live or exact quantitative condition map.

hotspots.label: LAND CONVERSION
hotspots.detail: Land conversion is a documented Amazon pressure category. Local attribution requires place- and time-specific evidence.

hotspots.label: EVIDENCE
hotspots.detail: Use HOW DO WE KNOW? to inspect the source record and limitation attached to the pressure node.

items.label: Pressure
items.note: Sourced category; local magnitude not inferred

items.label: Occurrence
items.note: Never treated as range or population

items.label: Time
items.note: No false live-state claim

response.title: Pressure is not the destination.
response.body: Compare response classes against the problem. A solution class is not evidence of delivery or impact.

hotspots.label: RESTORE
hotspots.detail: Restoration can be explored as a response class. Effectiveness depends on ecology, governance, permanence and local stewardship.

hotspots.label: PROTECT
hotspots.detail: Protection is a pathway class, not a generic outcome claim. A real project requires an accountable actor and evidence.

hotspots.label: MONITOR
hotspots.detail: Monitoring can strengthen evidence and accountability. Monitoring alone is not ecological recovery.

items.label: Restore
items.note: Habitat recovery pathway

items.label: Protect
items.note: Connectivity / habitat protection pathway

items.label: Monitor
items.note: Evidence / accountability pathway

actors.title: Solutions need accountable actors.
actors.body: Match each response to the actor roles capable of delivering it in place. Named organisations require separate verification before publication.
actors.audioLabel: HUMAN-SCALE PULSE + CANOPY BED · NO PARTNERSHIP SIGNAL

hotspots.label: STEWARDSHIP
hotspots.detail: Local and Indigenous stewardship is represented as an actor-role category only. No partnership or endorsement is implied.

hotspots.label: SCIENCE
hotspots.detail: Science and monitoring actors can establish evidence, but monitoring is not itself ecological recovery.

hotspots.label: DELIVERY
hotspots.detail: Delivery actors require verified competence, geography and project accountability before any action is offered.

items.label: Actor identity
items.note: Specific organisations remain fail-closed until verified

items.label: Actor fit
items.note: Solution + geography + capability

items.label: Partnership
items.note: Never inferred from a profile or reference

action.title: Action begins only when delivery is real.
action.body: The action path is Project → Actor → Unit → Evidence. If a verified Jaguar-linked unit does not exist, the interface says so instead of inventing one.
action.audioLabel: FORWARD MOTIF + LOW CANOPY BED · NO TRANSACTION SOUND

hotspots.label: PROJECT
hotspots.detail: A real action starts with a defined project and scope, not a generic donation button.

hotspots.label: ACTOR
hotspots.detail: The responsible actor must be verified before action can be presented as deliverable.

hotspots.label: IMPACT UNIT
hotspots.detail: No Jaguar-specific verified purchasable impact unit is asserted in this prototype. The gate remains visible rather than fabricated.

items.label: Project
items.note: Must have a defined scope and owner

items.label: Actor
items.note: Must be verified for capability + geography

items.label: Impact Unit
items.note: No Jaguar-specific verified unit active in this prototype

modules.label: Open AM4ZONIA mission
modules.state: MISSION CONTEXT · NOT A VERIFIED UNIT

proof.title: The journey does not end at a click.
proof.body: Proof closes the loop: what happened, where, who delivered it, what evidence exists, and what ecological result can honestly be claimed.

hotspots.label: WHERE
hotspots.detail: Reporting needs a place and time boundary before it can be interpreted.

hotspots.label: WHO
hotspots.detail: The delivery actor and its responsibility must be explicit.

hotspots.label: EVIDENCE
hotspots.detail: Evidence precedes any ecological outcome claim. Delivery evidence and ecological impact are not the same thing.

items.label: Delivery
items.note: What happened and who delivered it

items.label: Place + time
items.note: Where and when the action occurred

items.label: Ecological result
items.note: Claim only what monitoring supports
